outline: 342 Finding the Equation from the Graph

examples.question_text:
A bakery has fixed daily costs of $\$360$. Each cake costs $\$2$ to make and sells for $\$8$. Let $n$ be the number of cakes made and sold.
(a) Write equations for cost $C$ and revenue $R$.
(b) Find the break-even quantity and revenue algebraically.
(c) The bakery can sell at most $50$ cakes per day. Explain whether it can break even.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Fixed costs are added to the production cost.
$C=360+2n$
$R=8n$

(b) Set revenue equal to cost.
$\begin{align*}R&=C\\8n&=360+2n\\6n&=360\\n&=60\end{align*}$
Substitute $n=60$ into the revenue equation.
$\begin{align*}R&=8(60)\\&=480\end{align*}$
Break-even is $60$ cakes, with revenue of $\$480$.

(c) The maximum sales of $50$ cakes are below the break-even quantity of $60$. The bakery cannot break even under this limit.

examples.question_text:
A market stall has cost $C=250+3n$ and revenue $R=8n$, in dollars, where $n$ is the number of jars made and sold. Find the profit or loss when:
(a) $40$ jars are sold
(b) $70$ jars are sold.
examples.solution_text:
(a) For $n=40$:
$\begin{align*}R&=8(40)\\&=320\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}C&=250+3(40)\\&=370\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P&=R-C\\&=320-370\\&=-50\end{align*}$
The loss is $\$50$ because cost exceeds revenue.

(b) For $n=70$:
$\begin{align*}R&=8(70)\\&=560\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}C&=250+3(70)\\&=460\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}P&=R-C\\&=560-460\\&=100\end{align*}$
The profit is $\$100$ because revenue exceeds cost.

examples.question_text:
A small business makes bird feeders. Its fixed costs are $\$540$, each feeder costs $\$6$ to make, and each sells for $\$15$.
(a) Form the cost and revenue equations for $n$ feeders made and sold.
(b) Find how many feeders must be sold to earn a profit of $\$810$.
(c) Find the revenue at that sales volume.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The equations are:
$C=540+6n$
$R=15n$

(b) Set profit equal to $810$.
$\begin{align*}P&=R-C\\810&=15n-(540+6n)\\810&=9n-540\\1350&=9n\\n&=150\end{align*}$
Sell $150$ feeders to earn a profit of $\$810$.

(c) For $n=150$:
$\begin{align*}R&=15(150)\\&=2250\end{align*}$
The revenue is $\$2250$.

examples.derivation: The graph scales give R=6n and C=90+3n. Their intersection satisfies 6n=90+3n, giving n=30 and R=C=180, consistent with the graphical solution. At n=50, the plotted values are R=300 and C=240, so P=300-240=60: a $60 profit. Solution guides and markers match these coordinates; the question graph contains no answer annotations.

Fixed and variable costs give C=360+2n; sales give R=8n. Setting R=C gives 6n=360, hence n=60 and revenue 480. Maximum daily sales of 50 are below 60, so break-even is unattainable under the stated limit. No diagram is necessary.
At n=40, R=320 and C=250+120=370, giving P=-50: a $50 loss. At n=70, R=560 and C=250+210=460, giving P=100: a $100 profit. Both interpretations follow revenue minus cost. No diagram is necessary.

The models are C=540+6n and R=15n, so P=9n-540. Setting P=810 gives 9n=1350 and n=150. At that volume, R=2250 and C=1440, independently confirming profit 810. The target-profit method matches the supplied bird-house exercise. No diagram is necessary.
